---
title: "Sigma-clipping performance"
---

Sigma clipping keeps its numerical policy in a small Rust kernel used by both
the vector and axis-0 stack adapters.

- Caller-owned `Workspace` stores masks, rejection indices, statistical
  scratch, and optional restoration flags. `with_capacity` reserves buffers
  for reuse; inputs remain borrowed.
- The stack adapter reuses a column buffer and workspace across columns within
  each Rayon job. It scans sample/mask pairs directly, uses existing
  axis-order grain blocks, and takes the serial path for one block.
- Fused mean/median calls clip and reduce each column together. Valid final
  statistics are reused until the rejection mask changes; final means sum
  retained `f64` scratch in original order.
- MAD reuses retained-value scratch, populating it only when needed.
- Python normalizes dtype/contiguity once and skips matching mask reshapes.
  Stack work uses the order-statistic Rayon grain.

NaN and infinite samples are excluded. Centers and MAD are narrowed to input
dtype before threshold tests. Standard-deviation summation order is configured;
final means use sequential `f64`. MAD is `1.4826` times median absolute
deviation and ignores `ddof`. Strict `>` rejection preserves equality. Squared
residuals, limits, and variance sums can overflow; tiny values can underflow.
Invalid statistics leave masks unchanged; diagnostics report the last valid
spread.
